title: ANDS Studio overall product concept
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar branded "ANDS Studio" and the subtext "· guided ANDS filing", plus chips for "Help", "My dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry" and "Correspondence". The hero headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." Below it, body copy states: "An Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make. This walks you through it step by step — every term explained in plain language with the regulatory vocabulary kept precise, the right pathway chosen for your product, and your submission's readiness visible at every moment until it's ready to send." The main button is "Start my submission →", with a secondary link "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →" and a footnote: "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

Clicking "Start my submission →" opens a three-column layout: a step rail of journey stages on the left, the active step's card in the middle, and a right-hand panel showing a 3D "submission tower" of module tiles plus a readiness card. The top bar now shows a readiness chip — either "Ready to file" or a percentage like "34% ready" — and a "Start over" button. Returning later resumes your saved session ("Loading your filing…"). Regulatory acronyms carry plain-language tooltips, and the 3D tower can toggle to a plain checklist view of the same modules.

The validation the tool runs is scoped in plain terms. It is labeled a "Draft completeness check" that "checks presence and format only, not scientific adequacy or full eCTD technical validation," with the standing instruction to "Run Health Canada's eValidator before you transmit." A "What this does / does NOT check" toggle lists the structure/format rules it covers and, explicitly, what it does NOT check. Findings carry rule ids (CA-E-…/CA-W-…) and export to CSV or JSON with an embedded note that this is "NOT Health Canada review and NOT full eCTD technical validation." Export fails closed: a package cannot be produced from a dossier whose validation has not passed, and a worked-example / AI draft cannot reach a filing unreviewed.

On the "Account & security" page, the product surfaces its operations and identity posture. ANDS Studio is self-hosted: every service and database runs inside your own environment, and nothing leaves it except the packages you deliberately transmit to Health Canada. Every record is scoped to this workspace, and cross-workspace reads are refused at the API, not just hidden in the UI. You can add a time-based one-time code (TOTP) as a second factor via "Set up authenticator app →"; a separate section states the workspace-wide MFA mandate, a role permission matrix shows what your role can do, and a roadmap card dates not-yet-built capabilities. The page records honest limits plainly: single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) is not yet available — accounts are per-workspace. Every state change lands on an exportable, append-only audit event stream, downloadable as a regulatory inspection record.

Choosing "My dossiers" instead shows "Your product dossiers" with a "New dossier +" button. Creating one asks for "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"); entering the wrong format yields "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". Helper text explains Health Canada issues the ID via a REP request through your CESG account, and offers "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →". Deleting a dossier archives it to a recoverable trash rather than destroying it, restorable with undo. Inside a dossier the top bar swaps to tabs M1–M5 with pass/todo/not-applicable markers plus "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio" and "Journey" chips; the surrounding surfaces cover lifecycle operators and deficiency-response windows, bilingual and XML Product Monograph, multi-user collaboration, and a portfolio/PM layer showing owner, client and deadlines.
